title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G = GL(2,Ẑ) ⋉ Ẑ, where u ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) acts on Ẑ by u·λ = det(u)λ. Write u_0 for the image of u in G and ζ(λ) for the image of λ ∈ Ẑ. The determinant plays the role of a cyclotomic character: a Galois element acting on the Tate module of an elliptic curve acts on the 'central' Ẑ through the determinant.

The homomorphism (3). Grothendieck writes down a homomorphism from the central extension SL(2,Z)~ ≅ B_3 to G:
- ρ̃ ↦ ρ_0 ζ(−2) and σ̃ ↦ σ_0 ζ(3). Here σ has order 4 (the j=1728 point) and ρ has order 6 with ρ^3 = −1 (the j=0 point).
- In B_3 = ⟨a,b | a^2 = b^3⟩, take a = σ̃ and b = ρ̃^{−1}. The central element is ω̃_0 = ρ̃^{−3} = σ̃^2; in the image this is read as a double equality, not a product. It maps to ω_0 ζ(6) with ω_0 = −1.
- Its square ℓ'_0 = ω̃_0^2 generates the kernel of B_3 → SL(2,Z) and maps to ζ(12).
- So the Ẑ-coordinate is exactly the abelianization B_3 → Z (a ↦ 3, b ↦ 2, central generator ↦ 6). The map B_3 → SL(2,Z) × Z is therefore injective, because ℓ'_0 ↦ 12 ≠ 0. This is the familiar 12 of the Dedekind-eta / Rademacher picture.
- The last line, Γ̃_0 = τ̃' ↦ Γ_0, says the commutator subgroup lifts isomorphically.
- In effect G contains a 'congruence-type' completion SG = SL(2,Ẑ) × Ẑ of B_3. On SL this is a direct product, since det = 1. SG is enlarged by GL(2,Ẑ) acting through det, mimicking the arithmetic (Galois) action on the profinite π_1 of the moduli of elliptic curves with a tangential base point.

(4)–(5). SG is the inverse image of SL(2,Ẑ) and has centre {±1} × Ẑ. The Ẑ-factor of G acts trivially on SG by conjugation. Hence the conjugation action of G on SG factors through G/Ẑ ≅ GL(2,Ẑ), and α(x) = α̃xα̃^{-1} is well defined independently of the lift α̃.

(6). He considers β = (tσ + u)^{-1} with t² + u² = μ ∈ Ẑ^×, i.e. elements of the Cartan subgroup (Ẑ[i])^× centralizing σ, which in general have det μ ≠ 1. A struck alternative writes β = u̲ b^{-1} with u̲ = (μ λ; 0 1), relating to Aut(L_0).

(7). With a lift β̃, he forms η̃ = [β̃,σ̃] = β(σ̃)σ̃^{-1}. Since β commutes with σ in GL_2, η̃ is central. Explicitly β(σ̃) = σ_0 ζ(3·det β), so η̃ = ζ(3(det β − 1)) up to the convention μ vs μ^{-1); the page stops before stating this. He then begins computing σ(η̃) = σ̃(β̃) σ̃²(β̃)^{-1}, and the page breaks off.

Purpose. Together with the previous page, where he obtains ũ(ξ̃_0) = ξ(ν' − ν'' − 2ν) ξ̃_0 and linear constraints in ν_2, ν_3, ν_6, this computes the central ('Kummer-type') correction exponents. These govern how arithmetic/outer automorphisms act on lifts of the torsion elements σ, ρ of SL(2,Z) in the central extension B_3. It is the genus-1, one-point level of the Teichmüller tower, i.e. the B_3 ↔ SL(2,Z) relation underlying the elliptic Grothendieck–Teichmüller picture.
errors: Transcription '(ω̃_0 = ρ̃^{-3}σ̃^2)' must be read as ω̃_0 = ρ̃^{-3} = σ̃^2. Otherwise the image ω_0ζ(6) would be inconsistent: the product would map to ζ(12).
The stated quotient 'G/Ẑ^× ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)' should be G/Ẑ (quotient by the normal subgroup ζ(Ẑ)), not by Ẑ^×.
In (6), tσ+u has determinant t²+u² = μ, so β lies in GL(2,Ẑ), not in SL(2,Ẑ), unless μ = 1. The 'β ∈ Sl(2,Ẑ)' line is partly struck and inconsistent with the condition μ ∈ Ẑ^×.
The computation in (7) is unfinished; the expected central value of η̃ is never written down.

ideas.what: Embedding of B_3 = SL(2,Z)~ into SL(2,Z) × Z via (projection, abelianization), with σ̃ ↦ 3, ρ̃ ↦ −2, centre ↦ 6, kernel generator ↦ 12
ideas.modern_name: B_3 as universal central extension of SL(2,Z); the abelianization/Rademacher (eta-multiplier) homomorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Dedekind, Rademacher; Milnor's 'Introduction to algebraic K-theory' for the presentation of B_3 as central extension)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and SL(2,Z)~ only qualitatively

ideas.what: Group G = GL(2,Ẑ) ⋉ Ẑ with action through det, as an arithmetic envelope of the completed B_3, where outer automorphisms act on the centre through a cyclotomic-type character
ideas.modern_name: Congruence completion of B_3 with Galois/cyclotomic twist; arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} with tangential base point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Ihara; Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (elliptic GT, 1997); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion)

ideas.what: Commutator η̃ = [β̃, σ̃] for β in the Cartan subgroup centralizing σ, measuring the central correction (Kummer-type exponent) when twisting lifts of torsion elements
ideas.modern_name: Kummer cocycles for Galois action on profinite B_3 at elliptic points (j=0, 1728)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (explicit formulae for Galois action on π_1 of M_{1,1}), Lochak–Schneps

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an explicit 'congruence model' G = GL(2,Ẑ) ⋉_det Ẑ to compute the action of arithmetic automorphisms on lifts of the elliptic torsion elements in SL(2,Z)~. The aim is to pin down the central correction exponents (the ν's of the previous page). This is an early, hands-on version of the computations later done for the GT action on B_3 and π_1(M_{1,1}). The computation breaks off.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents Grothendieck's own approach (1981–82) to the B_3 / SL(2,Z)~ level of the Teichmüller tower and its arithmetic twisting. This predates Nakamura and Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps. It is of historical interest; the mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: A concrete, unpublished computation at the B_3 level of the Teichmüller tower with a cyclotomically twisted congruence model. It anticipates later work on GT action on B_3, but the content is elementary and incomplete, and later literature covers it.
transcription_corrections: 'G/Ẑ^× ≃ Gl(2,Ẑ)' is likely 'G/Ẑ ≃ Gl(2,Ẑ)'; the mark after Ẑ is probably not ×.
'centre μ×Ẑ': μ here denotes {±1} (= μ_2), the centre of SL(2,Ẑ).
In (6) the condition reads 't²+u² = μ ∈ Ẑ^*', with t, u ∈ Ẑ.
